title: The -cpu flag is removed — CoreDNS exits on it

detection.reason: container args of the Deployment/DaemonSet whose name contains coredns only — a CoreDNS image under another workload name is not scanned (the command lists those too), and a flag set through an entrypoint script or env is not scanned

quote: The `-cpu` flag is removed from this version.
remediation: Drop `-cpu` from the CoreDNS container args before upgrading; an unknown flag stops the binary at startup and takes cluster DNS down with it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.metadata.name | test("coredns")) or ([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("coredns")))) | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].args[]?] | any(test("^--?cpu"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name): " + ([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | join(" "))'  # each workload printed still passes -cpu, which CoreDNS 1.6+ rejects at startup; the rule itself reads workloads NAMED *coredns*, the command also lists a CoreDNS image under another name

title: kubernetes: resyncperiod is ignored (removed outright in 1.7)

detection.reason: read from the option KEY names the agent extracts inside each Corefile plugin block of every kube-system ConfigMap whose name contains coredns (agent 0.4.58+; older agents leave this NOT_DETECTABLE) — keys only, never values; import lines are not followed

remediation: Delete the line now: 1.6 accepts and ignores it, 1.7 refuses to parse it.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*resyncperiod\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed line = the option is still there

title: federation plugin moves out of tree — removed in 1.7.0

detection.reason: read from the directive names the agent extracts off every kube-system ConfigMap whose name contains coredns, each scanned as its own Corefile (an AKS coredns-custom fragment included) — names only, never values; import lines are not followed

remediation: Remove the federation block from the Corefile before 1.7.0. Kubernetes v1 federation itself is long retired, so the block is almost certainly vestigial; at 1.7.0 CoreDNS exits on the unknown directive.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*federation\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed line = the Corefile still loads federation, which 1.7.0 removes
coversNotes: In this release we have moved the federation plugin to github.com/coredns/federation, but
Note that 1.7.0 will contain a bunch of backward incompatible changes: the federation

title: Log lines no longer carry a timestamp

detection.reason: what parses CoreDNS log lines (a log pipeline's grok/regex) is not a Kubernetes object

quote: We've removed the time stamping from `pkg/log`
remediation: Log parsers that anchored on the leading timestamp of CoreDNS log lines need their pattern changed; the container runtime / journald timestamp is what remains.

title: Outgoing zone transfers move to the transfer plugin (file/auto/secondary/kubernetes convert in 1.8)

detection.reason: whether a plugin block carries a `transfer to` line is an option inside the block; the block's option keys are projected only by agent 0.4.58+ and the 1.8 rule reads them — this note is the announcement

quote: Plugins that already implement zone transfers are expected to move to it in the 1.7.0 release.
remediation: Plan to rewrite `transfer to …` lines inside file/auto/secondary/kubernetes blocks as a top-level `transfer { to … }` block; the conversion actually landed in 1.8.0 (see that rule).
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*transfer\\s+to\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed line is an in-block transfer that must move to the transfer plugin

title: 1.6.6 carries a DNS library security fix

detection.reason: a fix you get by running the release; nothing in the cluster's objects is configured differently

quote: The github.com/miekg/dns dependency has been updated to v1.1.25 to fix a DNS related security vulnerability
remediation: Upgrade to 1.6.6 or later to pick up the miekg/dns fix (miekg/dns#1043).
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("coredns"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name): " + ([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | join(" "))'  # prints every CoreDNS workload with its image tag

title: file: a missing zone file no longer stops CoreDNS starting

detection.reason: zone file paths are directive-line arguments, which are not collected

remediation: A typo'd or unmounted zone file used to fail startup loudly; from 1.6.0 CoreDNS starts and keeps retrying at each reload. Make sure something alerts on the file plugin's load errors if you relied on the crash.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*file\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # printed file directives now tolerate a missing zone file at startup

title: forward/grpc upstream health-check intervals are shorter by default

detection.reason: the health-check cadence is a default inside the binary; the Corefile's forward line is not collected beyond the directive name

remediation: Upstream resolvers see more frequent health probes from CoreDNS after 1.6.8. Rate-limited or metered upstreams should get an explicit `health_check` interval.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(forward|grpc)\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed upstream is probed more often unless health_check sets the interval

title: hosts: NODATA handling changed

detection.reason: answer-shape changes are request-time behaviour, not configuration

remediation: Clients querying a hosts-served name for a type the hosts plugin has no data for get a different (NODATA) answer shape; check split-horizon setups that relied on fallthrough here.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*hosts\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed hosts block answers unsupported types differently after 1.6.8
